appraisal_events.evidence: « Le Bloch-Guermantes ? Le familier des Guermantes ? »
appraisal_events.explanation: People who should know Bloch's humble origins now identify him only through his current elevated status as a Guermantes intimate; the narrator frames this as a memory-driven error, but the local social effect is that Bloch is now perceived as an established society figure, mirroring in reverse the earlier misrecognition of Swann.

appraisal_events.evidence: Bloch était entré en sautant comme une hyène... le visage presque effrayant, tout anxieux, d'un vieux Shylock attendant, tout grimé dans la coulisse, le moment d'entrer en scène
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator privately perceives Bloch's entrance and face in harshly unflattering, predatory terms, though he explicitly flags uncertainty about whether this troubling impression is objectively there or his own projection.

appraisal_events.evidence: il se fit présenter à moi... désirait faire ou refaire ma connaissance... on parlait de moi, pour de bien minces articles cependant, dans le milieu qu'il fréquentait
appraisal_events.explanation: A former enemy who had entirely forgotten their old rivalry now cordially seeks out the narrator, partly because the narrator's minor literary reputation now circulates in his circle, staging a quiet inclusion into valued regard from someone who once treated him with hostility.

status_effects.explanation: Bloch is locally perceived as an established Guermantes intimate by people who forget his earlier low standing, a modest elevation the narrator treats as an artifact of faulty social memory.
The narrator's private description casts Bloch as an anxious, predatory, performing figure, a sharply unflattering characterization even though its objectivity is left uncertain.
The narrator gains modest recognition and rapprochement from a former rival, reflecting his growing, if minor, social and literary standing.

ambiguities: Whether the narrator's 'Shylock'/'hyena' characterization of Bloch reflects objective perception or the narrator's own projection is left explicitly unresolved by the text ('soit qu'elle y survécût, soit que je l'y évoquasse').

The 'Bloch-Guermantes' label could be read either as a genuine (if partial) elevation of Bloch's social position or merely as another instance of the collective forgetting the narrator critiques throughout the passage; the text does not resolve which.
